Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions), Aisha Khan (CTO, Hearthline), Ben Torres (Platform), Marta Ruiz (Security), Jon Park (ML)
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming chat, steady-state token/sec, and hosting mode tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Agreed to run a small PoC benchmark with representative prompts and a streaming scenario; Redwood to share pricing and PoC plan.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
p95 latency targets and streaming behavior
KV cache and prefix caching effects
Quantization & model variants impact on throughput
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, data residency
Bench plan: token/sec benchmarks + canary traffic
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off - I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this deal. Laura and Diego with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: good thanks, busy day over here. excited to talk about the token throughput stuff and how to keep p95 under 300ms for our chat flows.
[00:15] Ben: quick note, our service is realtime-ish; we need streaming replies and p95 targets of 250-400ms depending on flow, higher tolerance for longer assistants.
[00:24] Laura: great, thanks. maybe start with your current setup and volumes? that helps us map hosted/dedicated sizing.
[00:30] Jon: sure - our baseline - about 120 rps peak across all users, but concurrency spikes to ~1.1k for short windows, most requests are short prompts ~30-80 tokens, a smaller conversational path streams 400-800 tokens.
[00:47] Diego: 1.1k concurrency spike, ok. do you use streaming for UI?
[00:52] Aisha: yes streaming for response token-by-token; UX needs first-token within 200-300ms ideally, and p95 for full response under 800ms in the longest flows.
[01:05] Laura: helpful. couple of clarifying q's: are you currently running on cloud GPUs? what model families?
[01:11] Ben: we use a mix - small internal models for classification, and a 30b open model on infra for the assistant. It's quantized to int8-ish but we hit memory and concurrency limits.
[01:22] Samir: okay, so tradeoff conversation: hosted Redwood gives same API and we manage capacity; dedicated gives reserved pools so spikes don't affect you; private gives you the control for VPC/KMS but requires more infra ops.
[01:35] Marta: security is big for us - HIPAA adjacency. we need KMS integrations, audit logs, SSO, and data residency guarantees. how do the options map to that?
[01:45] Laura: hosted can be SOC2 with customer keys via our KMS bridge, but if you need full on-prem or air-gapped, private is the path. dedicated gives network isolation and customer tenancy while still Redwood-managed. audit logs and RBAC are available across tiers.
[02:02] Aisha: can you give numbers on p95 and throughput? what's realistic for our token sizes?
[02:08] Laura: yeah, rough numbers: on a modern A100-style pool with optimized runtime, a 30b quantized model with streaming and prefix caching hits ~100-180 tokens/sec per instance depending on sequence length; p95 token latency depends on batching and active concurrency. for p95 end-to-end response latency on short prompts we'd target 200-450ms on dedicated with tuned batching and caching. hosted shared noisy neighbors can add variance but we have routing controls and fallback.
[02:37] Ben: hmm that tokens/sec per instance seems lower than we expected - we were budgeting 400-600 tokens/sec to keep latency tight.
[02:44] Laura: right—400-600 is possible with model variant + GPU type and aggressive quantization (4-bit) and higher memory; also depends on KV cache hit rates for conversation continuation. if you hit cold starts or cache misses, p95 jumps.
[02:58] Jon: can you explain the KV cache impact? our dialog model keeps long context.
[03:03] Diego: KV cache stores past key/value states so you don't recompute prefix tokens; with high hit rate, you only run the decoder steps, which increases tokens/sec significantly. if your clients start new sessions often, hit rate drops and cost/latency go up.
[03:19] Marta: transcription note - we need to be sure audit logs include token-level traces for compliance? is that available?
[03:25] Laura: yes we can surface token-level cost breakdown and redaction hooks; for PHI you can route through private with customer-managed KMS and disable logs at certain levels. we'll send the SOC2 doc.
[03:36] Aisha: ok, what's the best way to simulate our spikes for benchmarking?
[03:40] Samir: we recommend a two-phase PoC: a steady-state run that matches your steady 120 rps and an injection run to recreate the 1.1k concurrency spikes with short-lived sessions and streaming. we instrument with our test harness and measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cold-start behavior.
[03:56] Ben: are there known delta numbers for streaming vs non-streaming p95?
[04:00] Laura: streaming can reduce perceived latency (first-token) but increases end-to-end overhead for many small tokens; measured p95 for first-token often 120-280ms on dedicated, full-response p95 depends on response length. sometimes the first-token p95 is better than waiting for full generation, but network and client rendering matter.
[04:18] Jon: what about batching - can we tune to keep p95 under 400ms at 1k concurrency?
[04:23] Laura: batching improves throughput but can add head-of-line latency. our runtime uses continuous batching and latency-aware batching policies; for strict p95 we set small max-batch sizes and priority lanes. for your profile we'd suggest mixed lanes: low-latency lane for streaming UI and bulk lane for background tasks.
[04:41] Aisha: sounds good. how do fallbacks work if capacity is constrained? we can't have timeouts during surge.
[04:47] Diego: Redwood supports automatic fallback to smaller model variants or queued burst capacity on Dedicated; hosted has routing to cheaper model variants when primary is saturated. you can set SLOs to prefer lower latency or lower cost.
[05:00] Ben: any notes about quantization regressions on quality? our product team worries about hallucinations when going to 4-bit.
[05:06] Laura: yes quantization can cause small shifts; Redwood Optimize suggests model/profile combos and tracks evals against prompt sets to detect regression. part of the PoC we can run A/B quality checks.
[05:18] Marta: security again — SSO and SCIM? we require just-in-time provisioning and SAML.
[05:24] Samir: supported across tiers; for Private we can plug into your IdP directly inside the VPC. we'll include the SAML/SCIM integration guide.
[05:33] Aisha: and data residency — can you pin regionally?
[05:36] Laura: yes hosted has region pins and Dedicated/Private can be region locked or on-prem; we'll note compliance/residency options in the doc.
[05:45] Ben: okay cost sensitivity—if we go dedicated reserved pools, do we still pay per-token?
[05:50] Samir: Dedicated is commit pricing plus a usage overlay for bursts; reserved capacity lowers unit cost and gives predictable throughput. we'll share a model comparing hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated commit for your traffic profile.
[06:03] Jon: for the benchmark harness, do you need real PHI-like data? we can't share PHI of course.
[06:08] Laura: you can scrub/obfuscate or synthesize with the same token lengths and structure, that is ideal. length distribution and session reset patterns are the most important.
[06:18] Aisha: one more nit — we need p95 for first token in streaming under 250ms 90% of the time, and full response p95 below 800ms for 95% of production traffic. is that achievable?
[06:29] Laura: achievable with Dedicated plus prefix caching and tuned lanes; hosted may meet it but we recommend Dedicated for guaranteed SLOs at scale. private can too but requires ops work.
[06:40] Ben: what hardware is assumed in your estimates?
[06:43] Laura: estimates assume V100/A100 class GPUs and our optimized kernels; for higher token/sec you can pick H100 or more recent accelerators and we tune kernels accordingly.
[06:52] Jon: can we get a sample benchmark with our short-streaming prompts on an H100-backed dedicated node?
[06:56] Samir: yes, we can provision a benchmark run. Laura will draft the plan.
[07:00] Marta: on audit logs, can we turn on data retention shorter than 30 days? we need limited retention for PHI.
[07:06] Laura: yes you can configure retention and selective redaction; on private you control everything. we'll include options.
[07:14] Ben: curious—what about cold start penalties when traffic shifts to new model variant?
[07:18] Diego: cold starts vary but our runtime keeps warmed pools and supports pre-warming and predictive scaling; Dedicated reduces cold start frequency since capacity is reserved.
[07:28] Aisha: ok this is helpful. let's talk timeline - we want a PoC in 3 weeks if possible.
[07:33] Samir: works - our proposed schedule: collect prompt set & traces this week, Redwood sends benchmark plan by Tue (04/27), run PoC next week, analysis and quality A/B the week after.
[07:46] Ben: outstanding Q — latency variance during multi-region failover? we have users in EU and US.
[07:51] Laura: multi-region routing can add latency on failover; we advise region-local models for lowest p95 and cross-region fallback for resilience. we'll show routing policies.
[08:02] Jon: any constraints on model size for streaming?
[08:06] Laura: larger models affect memory and concurrency; if you need 30b with long contexts we'd recommend Dedicated with larger GPU memory profiles or sharded runtime.
[08:16] Marta: security checklist: SOC2 report, encryption in transit & at rest, customer-managed KMS, SAML/SCIM, audit logs, pen-test results. can you share those?
[08:28] Samir: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and pen-test summaries and the integration guides.
[08:33] Aisha: final ask: include clear pass/fail criteria for PoC: p95 targets, token/sec thresholds, and quality metric buckets.
[08:40] Laura: will do — we'll include objective success criteria, and sample dashboards for observability.
[08:46] Samir: great - recap next steps: Samir share pricing + SLA, Laura send benchmark plan, customer provide prompts + trace, schedule Marta SE deep-dive. any other items?
[08:57] Ben: none from me.
[09:00] Jon: thanks everyone.
[09:02] Samir: thanks — we'll follow up via email with artifacts. bye.
[09:05] (call ends)
notes: Customer is HIPAA-adjacent and leaning towards Dedicated for SLO guarantees
Priority: p95 first-token <250ms for streaming; full-response p95 <800ms
PoC will exercise 1.1k concurrency spike and 120 rps steady state
